summary: Smoothed (Wilder) moving average, 14 bars by default, a slow and steady line colored by its slope.
overview: The Smoothed Moving Average, also called RMA or Wilder's average, draws a slow and steady line over price. It is the same smoothing used inside RSI and ATR.
With Slope Trend Coloring on, the line is green while rising, red while falling and gray when flat. Length is 14 by default.
how: Each new value = (previous value x (N - 1) + latest price) / N. This works like an EMA with a smoothing share of 1 / N instead of 2 / (N + 1), so it reacts more slowly than an EMA of the same length.
The first value is seeded with a simple average.
use: Use it as a calm trend line that ignores small swings.
Some traders watch the color change as a sign the trend has turned.
Compare it with an EMA of the same length to see how much smoothing changes the picture.
Use it as a longer-term trend filter on lower timeframes.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It lags more than an EMA of the same length.
